summary: Accepted for host curation after an independent sealed replay, exact source-ownership review, exact scope comparison, and compact validation. None of the twelve cited Chinese passages asserts an office, festival, or appointment for Li Congke: they respectively record a general edict or annotation, a procedural register rule, assent to memorials, designation of the imperial birthday festival, Lü Qi’s appointment, Censorate procedure, and Yin Hui’s office. The candidate removes only the twelve unsupported p127 office claims while retaining Li Congke’s supported ruler identity, aliases, roles, active hint, surfaces, and every unrelated claim.

sourceEvidence.quote: 詔應曾受禦署官逐攝同一任正官
禦署官，疑是廢帝初舉兵時所置之官
請以正月二十三日皇帝誕慶日為千春節
呂琦守本官，充樞密院直學士
前任節度使、刺史、行軍副使

reviewedChanges.reason: Each removed row is an office assertion with subject p127 (Li Congke), but its cited sentence does not name or describe Li Congke as officeholder. s0236 and s0238 concern commissioned offices generally; s0256 a register rule; s0259, s0272, s0276, s0282 and s0284 imperial assent; s0271 the Thousand Springs festival designation; s0278 explicitly appoints Lü Qi; s0283 sets Censorate audience procedure; and s0286 explicitly identifies Hui as Xingzhou prefect. Removal is therefore source-faithful and does not retract any supported Li Congke fact.
